description: Single hardware source of truth. Every parameter has value, confirmed/unconfirmed status and source. Dimensions in metres, masses in kg, angles in degrees unless specified. World tabletop z=0. Asset paths exist only in the external versioned pack.

tabletop_z_m.source: Design rule: world z=0 is the tabletop top surface (scene.py contract).

bench_height_m.source: Conflicting historical floor-to-top values 0.885 and 0.801 m; measure in lab. Rendered CAD alignment uses bench_asset_top_z_m.

bench_height_alternatives_m.source: Conflict: Aldrin scene.py comment; jenga-rl layout.py.

bench_top_size_xy_m.source: Placeholder bench in scene.py; the real Vention top size is in the Vention CAD (vention.usd) and not measured.

workstation_xy_m.source: WORKSTATION_XY in settings.py: Vention offset relative to the robot at the origin, from Aldrin's source scene.

bench_scale.source: Preserved Vention USD metersPerUnit=0.01; convert centimetre asset coordinates to metre workcell stage.

bench_asset_top_z_m.source: CAD-only datum: bench/bench.usdc SHA256 34f75072eeb8667e0479cb3573b6df546e353b483712db25dfa5af42d04c9a60; default-prim-relative VentionAssembly_393251_v88_0/imported_PANEL_B2F52AEB2A0D_804849_271/Mesh_91 world bound top 80.0594045970318 cm. Not a lab floor-to-top measurement; bench_height_m remains unconfirmed.

panel_path.source: The bench's top panel (render mesh Mesh_91, collision box Mesh_91_collision/box in pack v2), relative to /World/Bench; the same panel bench_asset_top_z_m measures.

color_rgb.source: Kaleb (2026-11-13): the real tabletop is black. Vention sells black 1/4 in HDPE table panels; the pack's render material was a light rubber. Colour not measured.

roughness.source: Placeholder for a matte HDPE sheet; look only, no effect on physics.

static_friction.source: Placeholder for a wooden Jenga block on HDPE, equal to the block material. Measure with a tilt test: raise one end of the panel until a block starts to slide; static friction = tan(angle).

dynamic_friction.source: As above: the angle at which a sliding block keeps sliding at constant speed. MuJoCo (Newton) uses one sliding coefficient per pair; PhysX uses both.

default_static_friction.source: For every collider with no material of its own (arm, gripper links, bench frame): PhysX's default, so such parts behave the same on Newton, where an unbound collider otherwise gets mu 1.0 (isaacsim.physics.newton newton_config.py:99). Not measured.

combine_mode.source: MuJoCo (Newton) combines two geoms' friction by max (newton solvers/mujoco/kernels.py:162); PhysX is set to max on every material so each pair gets the same friction on both engines.

newton_friction.source: Newton reads one coefficient, dynamicFriction (newton import_usd.py:3982); the work cell sets it to the static value on Newton because Jenga depends mostly on when a block starts to slide. Sliding then runs about 0.05 grippier than on PhysX.

ur5e_links.source: Universal Robots ROS 2 description, config/ur5e/physical_parameters.yaml (rolling; sha256 0e58b89069d8d87b24cce0c2c02832d88de0f3229baf42916953ce1c71f0fa2d): link masses and CoMs in the URDF link frames the pack's robot uses; each tensor rotated by the file's inertia rotation into the link frame and decomposed into principal moments and axes. Masses match UR's DH article (UR5e table). Replaces the CB-series UR5 values the pack carried (4.0/3.7/8.393/2.275/1.219/1.219/0.1879).

rg2_links.source: Total 0.78 kg from the OnRobot RG2 datasheet v1.8 (https://onrobot.com/storage/datasheets/rg2/datasheet_rg2_v1.8_en.pdf, "Weight 0.78 [kg]"), split over the links by convex-hull volume of pack v2's collision hulls (uniform density); CoMs and principal moments from the same hulls with small off-diagonal terms dropped. The base CoM (0, 0.0002, 0.0641) agrees with OnRobot's own model (base 0.193 kg + body 0.464 kg, body 47.3 mm up). Whether 0.78 kg includes the Quick Changer tool side is not stated: weigh it.

mounting.value: Vention robot plate on the carriage plate of a Vention rail (all three in the bench asset)
mounting.source: Kaleb; photo of the base, 2026-11-14 (four screws into a blue square plate, on a larger dark hole-grid plate, on a rail along one long side of the table), and the bench asset itself (Vention's CAD, VentionAssembly_393251_v88, pack file bench/), which holds the same three parts under the robot: prims ST_RB_001_0002 (plate 180 x 180 x 22 mm), MO_LM_027_0001 (plate 268 x 268 mm) and the rail with its belt (MO_LM_024). The rail is a moving axis: see rail.

initial_joint_deg.source: Presentation pose; not a measured lab home pose.

placement.source: Height from the bench asset itself (Vention's CAD, VentionAssembly_393251_v88, pack file bench/): the top face of the robot plate ST_RB_001_0002 is 80.0 mm above the table top (its box spans z = 58 to 80 mm; the carriage plate below it 37 to 58 mm), centred within 1 mm of the robot's axis. Unconfirmed because it is the CAD's height, not a measurement in the lab: measure the base flange's underside above the table top. Until 2026-11-14 the base sat at 5 mm on a 5 mm proxy plate, inside these parts. Yaw 180 degrees about z (Kaleb, 2026-11-13): the shoulder faces the table, as on the real cell; the imported UR base_link faced away from it.

moving.source: Kaleb, 2026-11-14: the Vention rail under the UR5e really moves; the robot's base is a seventh axis. the lab's RISL_vention_ros (https://github.com/MaxlGao/RISL_vention_ros at commit ac9c7da23cf7daeacd5c9ecc37c7d5d699c1e53b, Apache-2.0) drives it. false builds the base fixed at the built pose, with the carriage as part of the scene.

actuator.value: Vention heavy-duty enclosed timing belt actuator, 1530 mm extrusion (MO-LM-027 family), with Vention robot plate ST-RB-001-0002 on its carriage
actuator.source: Identified from the bench asset (Vention's CAD of the lab's bench, VentionAssembly_393251_v88, in the private pack): carriage group MO_LM_027_0001 with a 268 x 268 mm gantry plate (MO_LM_025_0004), extrusion ST_EXT_007_0585_1530 (1530 mm), belt MO_LM_024_XXXX_1720, end blocks MO_LM_025_0001, motor and gearbox MO_SM_012_0001 at the +X end, 1777 mm overall. Vention, 'Enclosed Timing Belt Actuator' technical document (https://docs.vention.com/docs/enclosed-timing-belt-actuator) lists MO-LM-027-XXXX as the heavy-duty version (270 x 270 mm gantry, overall length = extrusion + 247.5 mm = 1777.5 mm) and names it for robot range extenders. Unconfirmed: read the part number on the actuator's label.

joint_name.source: Simulation: the prismatic joint between the fixed rail link and the carriage, first in the articulation's joint order.

axis_in_world.source: the bench asset (Vention's CAD of the lab's bench, VentionAssembly_393251_v88, in the private pack): the rail runs along the table's long edge, the cell's X axis, beside the table top's +Y edge (rail body from x = -0.890 to 0.887 m, y = -0.046 to 0.044 m); the motor is at the +X end. Matches the photos (rail along the table's long edge).

travel_m.source: Vention, 'Enclosed Timing Belt Actuator' technical document (https://docs.vention.com/docs/enclosed-timing-belt-actuator): travel of the heavy-duty version = extrusion length - 260 mm = 1270 mm for the 1530 mm extrusion; that includes 15 mm for the home and end sensors, so the hard stops are 1285 mm apart. The geometry in the bench asset (Vention's CAD of the lab's bench, VentionAssembly_393251_v88, in the private pack) agrees within 1 cm (1530 mm extrusion, 268 mm carriage: 1262 mm before the carriage passes the extrusion's ends). Unconfirmed for the lab's unit: the sensors can sit in any of four ports, so read the travel from the controller or measure it.

limits_m.source: Simulation: Vention's 1270 mm travel, centred on where the bench asset (Vention's CAD of the lab's bench, VentionAssembly_393251_v88, in the private pack) has the carriage (the middle of the extrusion within 1 mm), which is the pose the cell is built in. Inside what the geometry allows; not the lab's measured soft limits (Not found in the lab's five repositories (RISL_vention_ros ac9c7da2, RISL_ur 011539ab, RISL_onrobot_ros 7f86a05a, RISL_simulation d659f7d4, risl_assembly_workspace 82b9a510) or in Vention's public documentation).

default_position_m.source: The joint's zero is the cell's built pose: the carriage where the bench asset (Vention's CAD of the lab's bench, VentionAssembly_393251_v88, in the private pack) has it, the middle of the travel, with the robot's axis at the cell's origin. The real home position is not known. The lab's README example command is 650.0 mm, which is 15 mm from this pose if the real zero is at one end of the travel.

real_zero_at_joint_m.source: ASSUMPTION, not from any source: the real axis's zero (home) is at the -X end of the travel, the end away from the motor. Not found in the lab's five repositories (RISL_vention_ros ac9c7da2, RISL_ur 011539ab, RISL_onrobot_ros 7f86a05a, RISL_simulation d659f7d4, risl_assembly_workspace 82b9a510) or in Vention's public documentation: where the home sensor is. the lab's RISL_vention_ros (https://github.com/MaxlGao/RISL_vention_ros at commit ac9c7da23cf7daeacd5c9ecc37c7d5d699c1e53b, Apache-2.0) only shows that 0.0 mm is a reachable position (its test moves to 100.0 mm and back to 0.0). Read it on the real axis: home it and see where the carriage stops.

real_positive_direction.source: ASSUMPTION, not from any source: positive millimetres run toward +X (toward the motor). Not found in the lab's five repositories (RISL_vention_ros ac9c7da2, RISL_ur 011539ab, RISL_onrobot_ros 7f86a05a, RISL_simulation d659f7d4, risl_assembly_workspace 82b9a510) or in Vention's public documentation. -1 mirrors the mapping.

speed_m_s.source: Simulation choice, not the real value. Not found in the lab's five repositories (RISL_vention_ros ac9c7da2, RISL_ur 011539ab, RISL_onrobot_ros 7f86a05a, RISL_simulation d659f7d4, risl_assembly_workspace 82b9a510) or in Vention's public documentation (Vention gives performance curves, not one number; the lab's node sets no speed). Read the configured speed from the MachineMotion controller. Authored as the joint's velocity limit, which only PhysX applies.

acceleration_m_s2.source: Simulation choice, not the real value. Not found in the lab's five repositories (RISL_vention_ros ac9c7da2, RISL_ur 011539ab, RISL_onrobot_ros 7f86a05a, RISL_simulation d659f7d4, risl_assembly_workspace 82b9a510) or in Vention's public documentation. Read the configured acceleration from the MachineMotion controller. Used by callers that ramp the target; no engine applies it by itself.

max_force_n.source: Vention, 'Enclosed Timing Belt Actuator' technical document (https://docs.vention.com/docs/enclosed-timing-belt-actuator): maximum peak axial force (Fx) 1240 N. The position drive's force limit.

carriage_mass_kg.source: Estimate from the bench asset (Vention's CAD of the lab's bench, VentionAssembly_393251_v88, in the private pack): 1317 cm3 for the carriage group and 391 cm3 for the robot plate, as aluminium (2.7 g/cm3): 3.6 + 1.1 kg; bearings, screws and the belt clamp are not counted. Vention gives only the whole actuator's 27.31 kg. Weigh or ask Vention.

rail_mass_kg.source: Vention, 'Enclosed Timing Belt Actuator' technical document (https://docs.vention.com/docs/enclosed-timing-belt-actuator): 27.31 kg for the heavy-duty actuator with the 1530 mm extrusion, less the carriage estimate. The rail link is fixed to the world, so this mass moves nothing.

drive.source: Simulation: a position drive that holds the carriage (about 27 kg with the robot) within a fraction of a millimetre and settles without overshoot; on Newton dt^2 k / armature = 0.16 at 500 Hz against the explicit-spring limit of 4. Not a model of the real motor, gearbox or belt (208 mm per motor turn, backlash 0.25 mm in Vention's document).

carriage_mount.source: the bench asset (Vention's CAD of the lab's bench, VentionAssembly_393251_v88, in the private pack): the 90 x 90 mm rail's top is 35 mm above the table top, the carriage's gantry plate is 268 x 268 x 23 mm, Vention's robot plate on it is 180 x 180 x 22 mm with two locating pins, and its top face, where the robot's base sits, is 80 mm above the table top. The photo of the base (2026-11-14) shows the same stack and four screws through the base. The bolt pattern was not read from the CAD, and nothing was measured in the lab.

tool_axis.source: robot.py (flange-identity mount). The stack itself follows one switch, bota.mounted: false (the arm as it is) gives flange, Quick Changer, RG2; true puts an adapter plate, the Bota and a second adapter plate first. There is no separate order to edit (exts/workcell/workcell/stack.py).

mounted.source: Kaleb, 2026-11-14: the lab owns the sensor, but it is not mounted on the arm. The photos of the wrist taken that day show wrist 3's flange followed directly by the Quick Changer. Set true to build the sensor and its two adapter plates between the flange and the Quick Changer: the stack's order and lengths, the tool offset, the payload, the wrist camera's pose in tool0 and the source of the force/torque read all follow this one switch.

model.source: RISL_assembly_workspace auxiliary/bota_socket.json (product_name). Question for Kaleb (2026-11-14): he spoke of a sensor the lab just bought; if that is not this Rokubi with the connector on its side, this record, the dimensions and the pack's asset must be corrected.

diameter_m.source: Bota Systems' official STEP 'Rokubi/Medusa Gen 0 Series Side' (ROK-A000, https://shop.botasys.com/shop/rokubi-medusa-gen-0-series-kit-1877/document/180, listed on https://shop.botasys.com/shop/rokubi-medusa-gen-0-series-kit-1877; sha256 90cb4bd0551a8090428c7fa470b3c3bcb1cf3c7e60e8363cc976efd8a82c7063): body 48.0 mm across; the Rokubi datasheet says the same. The connector housing on the side reaches 37 mm from the axis.

length_m.source: Bota Systems' official STEP 'Rokubi/Medusa Gen 0 Series Side' (ROK-A000, https://shop.botasys.com/shop/rokubi-medusa-gen-0-series-kit-1877/document/180, listed on https://shop.botasys.com/shop/rokubi-medusa-gen-0-series-kit-1877; sha256 90cb4bd0551a8090428c7fa470b3c3bcb1cf3c7e60e8363cc976efd8a82c7063): 32.0 mm between the two faces; the Rokubi datasheet says the same. The adapter plates on both faces are separate: bota.robot_side_plate and bota.tool_side_plate.

mass_kg.source: Bota Rokubi BFT-ROKS-SER-M8 datasheet (serial version): weight 113 g. Excludes the adapter plates and the cable.

sensor_origin_along_axis_m.source: Bota's URDF and documentation: the wrench is expressed at the tool-side face, 32.0 mm from the robot-side face, same axes.

rate_hz.source: Simulation physics sampling rate, not a claimed real Bota output rate.

wrench_topic.source: Not published by the simulation; the name is the old twin's. The Bota driver's topic is not pinned in Max's sources: read it from the lab's bota_driver launch. The stock UR driver's /force_torque_sensor_broadcaster/wrench is the flange sensor's (flange_ft_sensor.wrench_topic), not the Bota's.

wrench_type.source: Existing twin publisher; wrench_utils.py in RISL_ur.

measurement.source: Simulation, when bota.mounted is true: the reaction at the fixed joint on the sensor's tool-side face (between the sensor and the adapter plate it holds), in the sensor frame; everything below the sensor hangs from it. A rigid-body joint reaction, not a calibrated hardware output; no noise or drift is modelled.

robot_side_plate.source: PLACEHOLDER, measure it: there is no drawing, part number or measurement of the lab's adapter plate, and Bota publishes none for this flange (its Universal Robots kit is built on the SensONE, which bolts to an ISO 9409-1-50 flange without adapters; the Rokubi's faces carry M3 patterns). The value is a solid aluminium disc of the UR5e tool flange's 63 mm diameter, 8 mm thick (2.7 g/cm3: 67 g). Built only when bota.mounted is true, as a labelled placeholder disc. This one sits between the UR5e's flange and the sensor.

tool_side_plate.source: PLACEHOLDER, measure it: there is no drawing, part number or measurement of the lab's adapter plate, and Bota publishes none for this flange (its Universal Robots kit is built on the SensONE, which bolts to an ISO 9409-1-50 flange without adapters; the Rokubi's faces carry M3 patterns). The value is a solid aluminium disc of the UR5e tool flange's 63 mm diameter, 8 mm thick (2.7 g/cm3: 67 g). Built only when bota.mounted is true, as a labelled placeholder disc. This one sits between the sensor and the Quick Changer.

model.value: Universal Robots UR5e built-in tool flange force/torque sensor
model.source: Kaleb, 2026-11-14: without the Bota, the cell's wrist force/torque reading is the UR5e's own sensor. Universal Robots UR5e technical details (https://www.universal-robots.com/media/1807465/ur5e_e-series_datasheets_web.pdf), 'F/T Sensor'.

force_range_n.source: Universal Robots UR5e technical details (https://www.universal-robots.com/media/1807465/ur5e_e-series_datasheets_web.pdf), 'F/T Sensor': force, x-y-z, range 50.0 N. Not modelled: the simulated reading has no range limit.

force_precision_n.source: Universal Robots UR5e technical details (https://www.universal-robots.com/media/1807465/ur5e_e-series_datasheets_web.pdf), 'F/T Sensor': force, x-y-z, precision 3.5 N. Not modelled: the simulated reading has no noise.

force_accuracy_n.source: Universal Robots UR5e technical details (https://www.universal-robots.com/media/1807465/ur5e_e-series_datasheets_web.pdf), 'F/T Sensor': force, x-y-z, accuracy 4.0 N. Not modelled; use it as the error bar when a real reading is compared with the simulated one.

torque_range_nm.source: Universal Robots UR5e technical details (https://www.universal-robots.com/media/1807465/ur5e_e-series_datasheets_web.pdf), 'F/T Sensor': torque, x-y-z, range 10.0 N m. Not modelled.

torque_precision_nm.source: Universal Robots UR5e technical details (https://www.universal-robots.com/media/1807465/ur5e_e-series_datasheets_web.pdf), 'F/T Sensor': torque, x-y-z, precision 0.2 N m. Not modelled.

torque_accuracy_nm.source: Universal Robots UR5e technical details (https://www.universal-robots.com/media/1807465/ur5e_e-series_datasheets_web.pdf), 'F/T Sensor': torque, x-y-z, accuracy 0.3 N m. Not modelled.

frame_id.source: The stock ur_robot_driver configuration (ur_controllers.yaml: force_torque_sensor_broadcaster with sensor_name tcp_fts_sensor and frame_id tool0). The lab's own files do not subscribe to this topic, so the lab's configuration is not confirmed. In the simulation the reading is expressed at the centre of the flange plane in tool0's axes (the pack's wrist_3_link/flange/tool0).

wrench_topic.source: The stock ur_robot_driver topic for the flange sensor. Not published by the simulation: read the simulated value with workcell__robot(action="wrench").

measurement.source: Simulation: the reaction at the fixed joint between wrist 3 and the first part bolted to the flange, at the centre of the flange plane, in tool0's axes: force and torque exerted on the tool by the arm, torque about the flange centre. Raw: at rest it holds the whole weight below the flange. The real controller reports the force at the tool centre point after subtracting the payload set on the pendant, so compare the two after removing the payload's weight, or with the pendant's payload set to zero. The real driver's sign convention has not been checked against this one. No noise, drift, range or accuracy limit is modelled.

model.value: OnRobot Quick Changer, robot side (the tool side is part of the RG2)
model.source: Kaleb; the photos of the wrist (2026-11-14) show the blue robot-side ring with its connector, and a small cable clip opposite it. OnRobot's official robot-side STEP 'Quick Changer Robot side' v2 (https://onrobot.com/storage/quick-changer-robot-side_v2_with_cable_holder.step, linked from https://onrobot.com/en/products/quick-changer; sha256 ac3cb44b90b27b172423400def5150a9af8b6e9338baf358f413118cbf5f38db).

standoff_m.source: OnRobot Quick Changer datasheet v2.0 (https://onrobot.com/storage/datasheets/quick-changers/datasheet_quick_changers_v2.0_en.pdf): 13.6 mm, 'Distance from Robot flange interface to OnRobot tool'. OnRobot's official robot-side STEP 'Quick Changer Robot side' v2 (https://onrobot.com/storage/quick-changer-robot-side_v2_with_cable_holder.step, linked from https://onrobot.com/en/products/quick-changer; sha256 ac3cb44b90b27b172423400def5150a9af8b6e9338baf358f413118cbf5f38db) agrees: 13.6 mm from the seat for the flange to the face toward the tool, 71 mm across. Replaces 15.92 mm, a CAD value of unknown origin carried over from the old twin.

mass_kg.source: OnRobot Quick Changer datasheet v2.0: Quick Changer (the robot side) 0.06 kg. The tool side (0.14 kg in the same table) is part of the RG2 and is taken to be in the RG2's 0.78 kg (rg2.datasheet_mass_kg). The lab's unit has not been weighed.

cog_in_part_m.source: Centre of volume of the parts of OnRobot's official robot-side STEP 'Quick Changer Robot side' v2 (https://onrobot.com/storage/quick-changer-robot-side_v2_with_cable_holder.step, linked from https://onrobot.com/en/products/quick-changer; sha256 ac3cb44b90b27b172423400def5150a9af8b6e9338baf358f413118cbf5f38db) that the pack keeps, as if of one density; x along the tool axis from the flange plane, then the flange frame's y and z.

datasheet_mass_kg.source: OnRobot RG2 datasheet v1.8 (https://onrobot.com/storage/datasheets/rg2/datasheet_rg2_v1.8_en.pdf): "Weight 0.78 [kg]" (v1.4 said 0.65). It does not say whether the Quick Changer tool side is included. OnRobot's RG2 STEP holds the Quick Changer's tool side as part of the gripper, so the 0.78 kg is taken to include it (unconfirmed): weigh the gripper on its tool side.

width_command_units_per_mm.source: Conflict: Max's rg_gripper.py sends the integer string straight to move_gripper in 0.1 mm units (0..1100); his README says millimetres. Code wins.

pad_gap_range_m.source: OnRobot's official RG2 STEP 'RG2 Tier 2 - 101631' (https://onrobot.com/storage/303_rg2_tool.step, linked from https://onrobot.com/en/products/rg2-finger-gripper), with the datasheet's 149 mm overall width fully open (OnRobot RG2 datasheet v1.8, section 1.3): the gap between the fingertips' rubber pads runs from 0 to 100.8 mm. The datasheet's 110 mm stroke is not reachable between these fingertips: the finger mounting faces are 123.6 mm apart fully open (the datasheet's 124), and each standard fingertip with its pad is 11.4 mm thick.

joint_limits_deg.source: OnRobot's official RG2 STEP 'RG2 Tier 2 - 101631' (https://onrobot.com/storage/303_rg2_tool.step, linked from https://onrobot.com/en/products/rg2-finger-gripper): finger_joint, the one driven joint. Lower: the rubber pads meet. Upper: the datasheet's 149 mm overall width. Joint zero is unchanged from pack v2: the outer arm 46.04 degrees from the approach axis, pads 75.3 mm apart. The fingertips move on an arc: they reach 38.1 mm further along the approach axis closed than fully open (16.8 mm from joint zero to closed).

driven_joint.source: The real RG2 has one motor. right_outer_knuckle_joint and the four inner joints follow finger_joint through NewtonMimicAPI at exactly 1 or -1 (the CAD's linkage is an exact parallelogram). Command finger_joint only.

cog_in_body_m.source: Computed, not a vendor value: the 0.78 kg split over the links as in inertials.rg2_links, with the fingers at joint zero (pads 75 mm apart), in the RG2 body frame (origin 2.5 mm on the robot's side of the flange plane, +Z toward the fingertips).

tcp_in_body_m.source: OnRobot's official RG2 STEP 'RG2 Tier 2 - 101631' (https://onrobot.com/storage/303_rg2_tool.step, linked from https://onrobot.com/en/products/rg2-finger-gripper): the centre of the fingertips' rubber pads with the pads together, 218.6 mm from the RG2 body frame's origin along the tool axis. The fingertips move along the tool axis as they open: 201.8 mm at joint zero (pads 75 mm apart) and 180.5 mm fully open; the fingertips' ends are 15.0 mm further.

surface.value: standard RG2 fingertips, wrapped in tape
surface.source: Kaleb, 2026-11-14, and the photos of the real gripper: the fingertips are OnRobot's standard ones, wrapped in tape. There are no add-on pads; the simulated grip is on the fingertips' own collision shapes. The tape itself is not modelled as geometry.

block_size_m.source: OnRobot's official RG2 STEP 'RG2 Tier 2 - 101631' (https://onrobot.com/storage/303_rg2_tool.step, linked from https://onrobot.com/en/products/rg2-finger-gripper): fingertip block 101791, 9.9 mm thick, 20.5 mm wide, 29.9 mm along the approach axis.

pad_size_m.source: OnRobot's official RG2 STEP 'RG2 Tier 2 - 101631' (https://onrobot.com/storage/303_rg2_tool.step, linked from https://onrobot.com/en/products/rg2-finger-gripper): the rubber pad on the fingertip's gripping face (part 100084, 1.5 mm), 20.5 x 29.9 mm. The datasheet names the material: EPDM.

static_friction.source: Estimate, no source found: cloth-backed tape on a wooden block. Applied to the fingertip collision shapes (the pack's FingertipTape physics material). Measure with a tilt test: lay a block on a taped fingertip surface and raise it until the block slides; static friction = tan(angle).

dynamic_friction.source: Estimate, as above: the angle at which a sliding block keeps sliding. MuJoCo (Newton) uses one sliding coefficient per pair; PhysX uses both.

fitted.source: Proposed printed load-cell tips, not confirmed installed hardware; standard RG2 has no built-in fingertip force sensor.

range_n.source: To_buy: 500 g nominal cell range. RG2 can exceed this: mechanical overload stops and force limiting required.

topic.source: To_buy: Proposed name, std_msgs/Float32MultiArray [left_N, right_N]; does not exist on the real robot until the Arduino node is written.

model.source: To_buy: Proposed bridge-output sensor; HX711-compatible. Confirm overload margin before buying.

cell_size_m.source: Packaging envelope only; vendor drawing and hole pattern required before fabrication.

body_size_m.source: Intel RealSense D400 Series Datasheet rev 017 (September 2023), table 3-51: D415 width 99, height 23, depth 20 mm (https://www.realsenseai.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Intel-RealSense-D400-Series-Datasheet-September-2023.pdf). Listed here as length, depth, height.

color_fov_deg.source: D415 RGB FOV used by Max (camera_model.py) and by the work cell's workspace camera.

resolution.source: Max's merged_localization.py opens the wrist D415 colour stream at 1280x720 (c_width, c_height) and builds its camera matrix from this size and the 69.4 x 42.5 degree field of view, with the principal point at the image centre. The real unit's factory intrinsics are not recorded here.

clipping_range_m.source: Render setting, not a D415 property. The near plane must lie between the camera's own body proxy (11.5 mm deep around the optical origin, or the view is black) and the RG2 body (nearer than the renderer's default 0.1 m, which draws it cut open). The real colour sensor has no near cut-off; its depth stream starts at about 0.3 m.

offset_in_rg2_m.source: Unconfirmed, estimated from photo and from Kaleb's two corrections on 2026-11-14 to the first comparison image, then one photo. (1) 'The camera is in line with the gripper', not off to one side: the D415's body is centred on the gripper's mid-plane, so the optical origin (the colour sensor) is 35 mm along the finger-opening axis, +Y of the RG2 body frame. (2) The real camera is 'further from the robot and higher up', on a longer arm than the first model had. With the sideways position fixed at zero, the photo of the real bracket (runs/ur5e-rg2-real2sim/reference/real_wrist_bracket.jpg in the workspace, not in this repository) puts the body's centre 127 mm behind the tool axis (two fits agree within 3 mm; it was 66 mm) and between 20 and 60 mm from the RG2 body frame's origin along the approach axis (it was 117 mm). This value is 127 mm behind the tool axis and 102 mm along the approach axis: the distance from the fit, and the height as far toward the wrist as the bracket model's arm shape allows (a plate level with or above the collar needs a different arm). So the modelled camera is still 40 to 80 mm lower than the fit says. PROVISIONAL: Kaleb will take better photos and hopes to get the bracket's own CAD file from Aldrin; replace all three numbers from those. Whether the body or the lens is the centred point is not measured.

rotation_in_rg2_deg.source: Unconfirmed, estimated from photo: one photo of the real bracket taken from below (Kaleb, 2026-11-14; runs/ur5e-rg2-real2sim/reference/real_wrist_bracket.jpg in the workspace, not in this repository). Extrinsic XYZ degrees in the RG2 body frame: [tilt, 0, -90]. With no tilt the camera looks along the gripper's approach axis (+Z) with its long axis along the finger-opening axis (Y): optical +x = RG2 -Y and optical +y (image down) = RG2 +X, away from the gripper, so the gripper is toward the top of the image. The first angle tilts the camera about its long axis so the optical axis leans toward the tool axis: 39 degrees. PROVISIONAL, and no longer the photo's own reading: the tilt was first fitted at 25 degrees (uncertainty about 8) with the camera 66 mm behind the tool axis, from the visible width of the camera's vent-slot side against its front and the direction of the plate's top edge. On 2026-11-14 the camera was moved to 127 mm behind the tool axis (offset_in_rg2_m), and at the height the bracket model allows a 25 degree tilt would look past the fingertips; 39 degrees keeps the optical axis crossing the tool axis at the same point as before, 40 mm beyond the fingertips, so the fingertips stay in the upper part of the image. If the real camera is higher up, as the photo fit says, 25 degrees does the same there. Measure the angle between the plate and the RG2's back face. The 180 degree turn about the optical axis (gripper toward the top) is read from the lens order on the glass (the colour sensor and left imager are at the +Y end), the USB-C cable leaving the other end and the unbroken row of vent slots on the side facing the gripper (the top of the D415: the underside has the 1/4-20 hole, https://www.realsenseai.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Intel-RealSense-D400-Series-Datasheet-September-2023.pdf figure 10-8). The USD camera looks along -Z, so the builder adds Rx(180) internally.

mount_position.value: clamped to the RG2 body, off its back face
mount_position.source: one photo of the real bracket taken from below (Kaleb, 2026-11-14; runs/ur5e-rg2-real2sim/reference/real_wrist_bracket.jpg in the workspace, not in this repository): a two-piece printed clamp around the RG2 body below the gripper's own mounting bracket, with four cross bolts; a truss arm holds a flat plate behind the D415 off the face opposite the AprilTag, tilted so the camera looks at the fingertips. It is not a plate between flange faces, so the tool stack and the tool kinematics are unchanged, and the camera turns with the gripper. Before the bracket was fitted the camera was described as under the wrist.

bracket_mass_kg.source: Estimate, weigh it with its screws: the model in exts/workcell/cad/rg2_camera_bracket.py has 99.1 cm3 of solid (123 g in solid PLA at 1.24 g/cm3); about 80 g as printed with infill, plus four M4 bolts and nuts (about 20 g). Added to the RG2 body's mass in the simulation, at bracket_cog_in_rg2_m, so the bracket and the camera are in the simulated force/torque reading as they are on the real arm.

key_direction.source: Placeholder demo preset, not the lab's lighting. The direction the key light travels in the world frame: 35 degrees from vertical, from beyond the table's far edge and to one side, toward the robot. Straight down, an object resting on the bench casts its shadow under itself and none shows; this way objects on the bench shadow the bench and each other, and the arm's shadow falls toward the rail.

rail_position_command.source: the lab's RISL_vention_ros (https://github.com/MaxlGao/RISL_vention_ros at commit ac9c7da23cf7daeacd5c9ecc37c7d5d699c1e53b, Apache-2.0), vention_socket_control.py: subscribes to this topic, sends the value as an absolute move of axis 1 in millimetres and polls isReady and isBusy; its README's example is 650.0. Not subscribed by the simulation. The package states no travel limits, speed, acceleration, homing or direction. Vention's current socket document (https://docs.vention.com/docs/application-programming-interface-low-level-sockets-for-machinemotion, MachineMotion 3.1 and newer) gives port 9999 and millimetres, mm/s and mm/s2, and says homing moves toward the home sensor and resets zero there; the older command set the lab's node uses was not found in Vention's public documentation.

Which face is toward the tool (taken: the sensing element) and where the connector points about the axis are not confirmed for the lab's unit. Not built while bota.mounted is false.

quick_changer.source: OnRobot's official robot-side STEP 'Quick Changer Robot side' v2 (https://onrobot.com/storage/quick-changer-robot-side_v2_with_cable_holder.step, linked from https://onrobot.com/en/products/quick-changer; sha256 ac3cb44b90b27b172423400def5150a9af8b6e9338baf358f413118cbf5f38db), converted for the private pack (scripts/workcell_stack_assets.py): origin on the flange plane, +X along the tool axis, turned about it as OnRobot's RG2 STEP shows it on the gripper (connector on the RG2's finger-opening axis). The large cable holder of the STEP is left out: the photos show the connector free.

rg2.source: CPU inspection of private ur5e-jenga-workcell/v1 USD prims; physical inlet pose and roll not measured. Roll about the tool axis, from photos, confirm on the robot (2026-11-14): the RG2 is mounted with its front face (logo, AprilTag, the two M3 holes) on the same side as wrist 3's M8 tool connector. Evidence: (1) the photos of the wrist before the camera bracket was fitted (before_IMG_9206_wrist_stack.jpg, before_IMG_9213_wrist3_qc_rg2.jpg, and before_IMG_9212_rg2_front.jpg for the front face; in the workspace's runs/ur5e-rg2-real2sim/reference, not in this repository) show the connector, with its cable, and the logo both facing the camera. (2) In the pack's robot the connector is at tool0 -Y: prim wrist_3_link/visuals/wrist3/mesh has its one bump outside the 38 mm housing radius at (x, y) = (-0.002, -0.0435) m in tool0, between 30 and 40 mm behind the flange face. Universal Robots describes the tool frame the same way ("Y is away from the Tool connector, and Z is normal to the tool flange", https://forum.universal-robots.com/t/base-coordinate-system-documentation/140); no flange drawing that marks the axes was found. (3) The RG2's front face is the body's -X in the pack (the face with the pair of M3 holes of the OnRobot RG2 datasheet v1.8 front view). So the front face must point along tool0 -Y: mount_pose orientation (0, 0.7071, 0, 0.7071), the inlet's +X along the body's +Z as before and turned half a turn about it. Until 2026-11-14 it was (0.7071, 0, -0.7071, 0), which put the front face at tool0 +Y and the wrist camera, on the back face, on the tool0 -Y side: below the tool axis and inside the bench at the pose the cell is built in (every joint at zero). Position along the tool axis (2026-11-14): OnRobot's RG2 STEP holds the Quick Changer's robot side in place on the gripper. In the RG2 body frame the seat for the robot's flange is at z = 2.5 mm and the robot side's face toward the tool at z = 16.1 mm; the stack puts the RG2's inlet there, quick_changer.standoff_m (13.6 mm) after the part before it.

base_plate.source: CPU inspection of private ur5e-jenga-workcell/v1 USD prims; physical inlet pose and roll not measured

overhead_shelf.source: Derived from pack proxy dimensions (8 mm shelf): sits on the back of the tilted camera body; rotated 90 degrees about Z so its 0.1 m side runs along the D415 long axis. Not a measured assembly.

overhead_release.source: Derived from pack proxy dimensions (12 mm release plate): sits on the shelf, under the gantry beam. Not a measured assembly.

rail_carriage.source: Pack v3: the carriage of the bench's linear axis and the robot plate on it, split out of the bench asset (scripts/workcell_rail_assets.py); origin at the robot's base, the world's axes.

present.source: The bench asset already holds the real mounting plates under the robot (robot.mounting), so the separate 5 mm proxy plate is not built. true builds it again at placement, for a cell whose bench has no plate.

placement.source: Only used when base_plate.present is true. Candidate pack plate is 5 mm thick; provisional position below robot base, not lab measurement. Photo evidence, 2026-11-14: the robot base is bolted with four screws to a blue anodised square adapter plate, which sits on a larger dark Vention hole-grid plate, which sits on a Vention rail running along one long side of the table; the black table top is beside the rail and lower than the plate. So the real base is above the table top by an amount this single 5 mm plate does not represent; nothing was measured from the photos.

physics_hz.source: Live Newton tower check (scripts/smoke/newton_checks.py) and the 2026-11-13 work-cell probe: the tower holds at 500 Hz and collapses at 250.

impratio.source: 2026-11-13 work-cell Newton probe: without impratio 10 the top layer crept 0.4 mm/s.

drives.source: Chosen 2026-11-14 for Newton's MuJoCo-Warp at 500 Hz: armature 0.1 kg m^2 on every arm joint (as MuJoCo Menagerie's UR5e), stiffness so that dt^2 k / armature <= 2 against the explicit-spring limit of at least 4, damping near critical; validated live, see the work cell README.

robot_materials.source: Looks only, read off the photos of the real arm (2026-11-14): grey matte link tubes, silver aluminium joint housings and base, light blue caps. Applied to the robot asset's own materials on the stage; nothing here reaches the physics.
